bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

When discussing the **Bridget Brennan salary**, it's important to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage and the higher rates set by modern awards. The Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) provide the minimum pay rates for full-time, part-time, and casual employees under each award. These guides are updated after each Annual Wage Review, with the latest increase taking effect from 1 July 2026.

### The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This rate applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. For casual employees, a 25% loading brings the minimum to $33.05 per hour. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the Pay and Conditions Tool are the authoritative sources for these figures.

### Award Minimum Wages and Casual Loading

Award minimum wages are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage and vary by industry and classification. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains the calculated minimum rates, allowances, overtime, and penalty rates for each award. For example, a retail employee under the General Retail Industry Award may have a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage, plus additional penalty rates for evening or weekend work.

Casual loading of 25% is applied on top of the base award rate, not on top of a rate that already includes loading. When using the timesheet on this site, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to the base hourly rate you enter. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Converting Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, multiply the hourly rate by hours per week by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,253.44 per year (approximately).

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a standard estimate used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax Considerations

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is weekly pay × 2. For the National Minimum Wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly pay is $2,009.80 before tax.

Tax is withheld using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of generally 2%. The Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are from 2025–26, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. For a single person earning $52,253, the tax would be approximately $5,092 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a take-home pay of about $46,116 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised estimate.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the 2026–27 year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So if your annual salary is $52,253, your employer contributes an additional $6,270.36 in super, provided your earnings are below the cap. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### The Role of Pay Guides and the Modern Awards Pay Database

The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides and the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database are essential tools for determining correct pay. The database includes spreadsheets for awards, classifications, wage-related allowances, expense-related allowances, and penalty rates. Employers and employees can use these to ensure compliance. For a quick reference, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

When comparing the Bridget Brennan salary to award rates, remember that award rates often include additional entitlements such as annual leave loading, penalty rates, and allowances. An annualised wage arrangement may cover these entitlements in a fixed amount, but it must be reviewed annually to ensure the employee is not worse off.

In summary, the National Minimum Wage provides a floor, but most employees are covered by an award that sets higher rates. Always check the applicable award and use the official pay guides to confirm your correct pay.
